statement.p: Find the exact global maximum and minimum values of the function g(x) = 6 x - x^2 - 7 if its domain is all real numbers.

p.em: if there is no global maximum or global minimum for this function.)

static.solution:
g'(x)=0: g'(x) = 6 - 2x = 0, so x = 3. Since g'(x)>0 for x\lt 3 and g'(x)\lt 0 for x>3, the critical point at x=3 is a local maximum.
As x\to\pm \infty, the value of g(x)\to-\infty. Thus, the local maximum at x=3 is a global maximum of g(3)=6 \cdot 3 - 3^2 - 7 = 2. There is no global minimum.
